# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b92 — prevent Lovelace scroll-to-top glitches

Beta92 is a **frontend-only** patch building directly on the tested and
published Beta91 release. It responds to a real recording where the user was
scrolling through an expanded bedroom controller and the entire Lovelace view
suddenly jumped to the top with no user interaction.

## Fix

- **Restore page-level scroll after normal in-place card updates.** Beta91's
  stable DOM changed the card only *inside* the existing `ha-card`, but the
  inherited scroll recovery still only ran when the whole `ha-card` was
  replaced. This left large, unexpected dashboard scroll resets uncorrected.
- Capture scrollable Home Assistant ancestors across up to 80 DOM/shadow
  ancestors. On every actual in-place reconciliation, detect **large upward
  scroll displacements**, rather than fighting small, legitimate browser
  scroll-anchor adjustments.
- Rescue unexpected jumps synchronously and on the following two layout
  frames. Abort scheduled correction on a newly observed user scroll gesture.
- Preserve room/device expansion, controller links, focused inputs, information
  popovers and sibling dashboard cards. Do not impose auto-scroll to the card.
- Preserve the full-replacement fallback for temporary data-loading or error
  states, with no new polling, device commands or physical controls.

## Safety and regression verification

Real Chromium browser tests reproduce the observed jump in a three-column
dashboard with a shadow-root Lovelace scroller, for both synchronous and
next-frame layout reset timing, while checking stable sibling card identity.
The previous Beta87–91 card tests and all Beta91 physical actuator, dehumidifier
PWM, PID persistence, native command ACK/retry, window and power dwell tests
remain in release validation.

**No physical device-control or PID Python source is changed.** Existing
Beta91 dry/off dehumidification, safety timing, power-switch and restart
continuity behavior is retained.

## Install

Update the HACS prerelease to **v0.6.0b92**, restart Home Assistant if HACS
requires it, and **hard-refresh the browser** to replace the cached frontend
JavaScript. Real user environment validation remains distinct from the
automated regression tests.
